prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs. A few quick questions will let me give a targeted recommendation:

- Do you need an individual/family plan on the ACA marketplace, short-term coverage, or something else (eg, dental, vision, supplemental)?
- Are you looking for a local in-person broker in Kansas City, MO, or are you OK with a phone/online broker?
- Do you have a preferred budget or are you primarily looking for maximum coverage?
- Any special circumstances (pre-existing conditions, expecting a child, irregular income, Medicare eligibility soon)?

While you answer, here are practical tips and what to look for in a broker for someone self-employed:

What to look for in a broker
- Experience with ACA marketplace plans and premium tax credits (so they can tell you whether you qualify for subsidies).
- Familiarity with self-employed income issues (how to report variable income for subsidies, SE tax, etc.).
- Independent or multi-carrier access (not captive to a single insurer) so they can compare multiple carriers.
- Transparent about fees and commissions (ask whether they charge a broker fee and how they’re paid).
- Year-round service (not just during open enrollment) — important if your income or situation changes mid-year.
- Good reviews and licensed in Missouri — verify on the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance site.
- Willingness to provide written quotes and to walk you through costs (premiums, deductibles, OOP max, networks).

Where to find and verify brokers
- Search for independent health insurance brokers in Kansas City, MO (Google, Yelp, LinkedIn).
- Check licensing and complaint history on the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance site.
- For ACA enrollment specifically, you can use healthcare.gov to enroll or work with a certified Marketplace agent or assister.

Quick options to consider
- Local independent brokers/agents in Kansas City who specialize in individual and small-business markets (look for ones advertising ACA/individual plans and self-employed clients).
- National online marketplaces like eHealth or Stride (good for price-shopping if you’re comfortable doing it online).
- If you want in-person help and personalized planning, pick a well-reviewed independent broker who explicitly mentions marketplace experience and self-employment.

If you want, I can:
- Search and return a short list (3–5) of highly rated Kansas City, MO brokers who specialize in self-employed/individual plans, including contact info and pros/cons; or
- Recommend specific online brokers/marketplaces that match your preferences.

Tell me the answers to the questions above and I’ll find the best matches for you.
